newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare gains after record high start.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare gains after record high start.

text.p: German shares pared early gains on Thursday after opening bourse trade at another record high, boosted by gains in the banking sector and continuing a rally begun on Tuesday.
But dealers said the DAX index of 30 leading shares was still aiming for the technical and psychological level of 2,800 points and said it should reach that level this week.
The blue-chip DAX index touched an all-time bourse high of 2,785.16 points in early dealings, then pared gains to stand up 1.57 points to 2,775 points.
German government bond strength and another record close on Wall Street were also supporting the market, dealers said.

But the morning's main action was in the banking sector, with over three million Deutsche Bank AG shares and almost three million Commerzbank AG shares changing hands in computer trade Over a million Commerzbank shares were also traded in bourse dealings.
Deutsche was up 1.60 marks at 72.25 marks. Commerzbank jumped to a new year high of 37.38 marks in IBIS trade and was up almost four percent or 1.40 marks at 36.65 marks in bourse dealings.

Traders said the whole banking sector was boosted by talk of mergers, which have been rife in the sector since July when Deutsche Bank AG said it had amassed a 5.21 percent stake in Munich-based rival Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
"It's the old merger story," said one dealer.

But Commerzbank moved to quash merger speculation, saying it saw no one single large investor buying up the group's shares and said the strong rise in its share price was largely due to the fact that the shares were earlier undervalued.
Shares in Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, which had been lower after the bank announced higher nine month results, were pulled up as the rest of the banking sector climbed.
The stock was up 63 pfennigs at 47.36 marks.

Outside of the banking sector, shares in national airline Lufthansa AG were amongst the major movers, falling 22 pfennigs to 20.30 marks, after news that the European Commission had approved sales of more shares in the company.
